note.headline: Alphabet slips toward 296 support; cash flow still weak, price above fair value

summary.thesis: Alphabet's sales are speeding up and margins are rising, but free cash flow has collapsed and forecasts are falling, so the price of 295.77 still sits above what the cash and its own history support.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price sits between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Buy near 282.31; add in the 271.77–277.07 support zone

note.happening: Alphabet fell 0.98% to 295.77. That puts it inside a nearby price zone at 293.72–296.49, just under resistance at 300.07–305.86, and below its 20-day (303.42), 50-day (328.19) and 200-day (338.2) averages. Today's news is minor: The Verge reported that the new Apple TV has a YouTube problem, and a speculative CNBC piece discussed founder transitions. No earnings date is in the data.
note.business: The parts that change the business are mixed. Demand is strong. Quarterly sales grew 24.65% from a year ago, up from 21.79% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 33.32% from 32.19%. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow, the cash left after paying for operations and investment, fell to 19.7B over twelve months from 73.6B. That leaves only 4.19 cents of each sales dollar. The filings also flag that reported profit leans on one-off gains: net margin is 50.03%, above the 33.32% operating margin, so underlying earnings are lower than the headline number. Analysts have cut this year's EPS (earnings per share) estimate by 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's 14.97 sits below this year's 19.56. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 139.0B. Today's news is about sentiment only. A YouTube issue on one Apple device and a story about founders do not change demand, margins or cash.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply, and one assumption drives the gap. A discounted cash flow model values the business on the cash it produces, and it starts from today's free cash flow of 19.7B. On that base it gives 26.28 to 72.2 per share, with 52.56 in the middle. Even with a 30% starting growth rate it reaches only 79.03. So at 295.77, the price assumes cash flow will come back to a much higher level. Against its own history, price-to-sales (price divided by sales per share) gives 234.35 low, 282.31 middle and 375.22 high. The current 7.8 is at the 54.0th percentile of its own five-year range but above the peer median of 5.4. On earnings the stock looks cheaper: 15.5 times trailing EPS. But that rises to 19.8 times next year's estimate, and trailing EPS includes one-off gains. My range is 234.35 to 282.31. The price sits above it.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers from 19.7B toward the prior 73.6B once the current investment cycle pays off; if it stays near 19.7B, even 234.35 is generous.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 24.65% a year ago-on-year in the latest quarter versus 21.79% two quarters ago.
Operating margin rose to 33.32% from 32.19%, so growth is not coming at the cost of profitability.
Net cash of 139.0B gives room to keep investing through a weak cash-flow stretch.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 19.7B from 73.6B, and that is the base the cash-flow valuation of 52.56 rests on.
Analysts cut this year's EPS estimate by 5.2% in 30 days, and next year's estimate implies -23% EPS growth.
Price-to-sales of 7.8 is above the peer median of 5.4, and the filings note the price needs about 37% a year growth versus 17% delivered over 3 years.

levels.what: The middle of its own-history price-to-sales range and the top of my fair-value range; a first buy level.
Top of the 271.77–277.07 support zone, tested 3 times; a level to add at.
Low end of the own-history range, which leaves room for error if free cash flow stays near 19.7B.

longterm.why: The business earns a quality grade of B, but 295.77 sits above my 234.35–282.31 range while earnings forecasts keep falling. Buying at 282.31 or lower improves the trade-off.

swing.why: The price is in a range, below falling 20-day and 50-day averages, and caught between support at 293.72–296.49 and resistance at 300.07–305.86. That gap is too narrow for a clean entry with a sensible stop and target.

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data, so forecast revisions and price levels set the timing. Options price a move of about 4.3% by Nov 20 and 8.2% by Dec 18. The 290.0 put strike holds the most open put contracts (18375), which marks a level options traders have positioned around.

change_mind: A daily close above 314.7, the top of the 309.73–314.7 resistance zone (5 touches), would end the range and support moving to a long-term buy closer to the current price.
Twelve-month free cash flow climbing back toward 73.6B from 19.7B would lift the cash-flow value and narrow the gap with the 282.31 own-history value.
A close below 271.77, the bottom of the support zone, would move the buy level down to 234.35.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The price slipped to 295.77 but stays above my 282.31 ceiling, and this year's EPS estimate still sits 5.2% below where it was 30 days ago.
